claims.explanation: Rivaroxaban is a factor Xa (F10) inhibitor, and its antiproliferative selectivity in this screen most plausibly reflects dependence on coagulation-factor/F10 signaling or on the PAR-mediated thrombin/FXa axis in a subset of tumor lines, rather than a broad cytotoxic effect. The pattern is not explained by any single common driver mutation; instead, sensitive lines are enriched for RAS/RTK-MAPK pathway activation (NRAS, KRAS, EGFR, BRAF, ALK, ERBB3, NF1 loss) and squamous/neuroendocrine-like lineages, while many resistant lines carry PIK3CA/PTEN alterations or mesenchymal/ARID1A contexts. Because the transcriptional signature is weak and resembles warfarin, the effect is likely indirect and context-dependent, so the features below are proposed as testable correlates rather than established

features.basis: Drug target; lines with higher F10/FXa pathway activity may be more dependent on rivaroxaban-sensitive signaling
Observed enrichment of KRAS-mutant lines among sensitive (NCIH1792, LS1034, HS766T)
Observed in sensitive NCIH1299; RAS-MAPK activation may increase dependence on FXa/PAR signaling
Observed in sensitive melanoma lines (WM793, LOXIMVI) but also in resistant lines, so weaker
Observed in sensitive KNS81, NCIH1650, KYSE270; EGFR-driven lines may be more responsive
Observed in sensitive NCIH2452 mesothelioma
Observed in sensitive BICR6, LOXIMVI, KALS1; NF1 loss activates RAS-MAPK
Enriched in resistant lines (HGC27, HCC1954, KYSE510) and some sensitive lines, suggesting PI3K activation may buffer FXa dependence
Observed in resistant BT549, UACC62, FTC133, TE4; PTEN loss may reduce sensitivity
Frequent in resistant lines (SW1088, SUIT2, MHHNB11) and some sensitive lines, but chromatin remodeling loss may blunt response
Very common in both groups, so not selective; included only as a weak negative correlate
Observed in sensitive COV434 and KYSE270, but also in resistant OV7; weak evidence
